result.reason: The redline adds the required frequency, 30-day notice, business-hours, independence/confidentiality, and cost allocation concepts. However, it does not fully reach the preferred position: the cost-shifting trigger remains any “discrepancy” above 5%, rather than an underpayment exceeding 5%, and the no-access restriction applies only to Licensor, not expressly to the auditor conducting the audit. The added non-interference requirement is also beyond the stated playbook position, so the revision is not strictly minimal. Otherwise, it preserves the audit’s commercial purpose and is generally professionally drafted, although placing the cost paragraph before subsection (b) is awkward.
